h1: The Impact of Playground Equipment on Property Value

props.title: The Impact of Playground Equipment on Property Value
props.summaryText: Why a good play area helps sell homes, why a neglected one does the opposite, and what builders and societies should invest in to protect the value of a project.
props.author: ananya-kulkarni
props.imageAlt: Tepee play towers with slides and a net climber at a residential project in Gujarat

takeaways.text: Families with children shortlist projects partly on their amenities, and the play area is among the most visible.
A play area helps value only if it still looks good years after handover; a faded, rusting one hurts it.
Place the play area where buyers see it on a site visit and where residents can watch from home.
Choose equipment and materials that the society can maintain easily after handover.

faq.a: A well-designed, well-maintained play area makes a residential project more attractive to families, who are a large share of home buyers, and supports demand and resale. The effect depends on quality: a neglected play area can count against a project.

faq.q: What amenities do home buyers with children look for?
faq.a: A safe, visible play area with equipment for different ages, open space for running and cycling, shade and seating for parents, and often an outdoor gym or sports area. Many also look at whether the amenities are maintained in older projects by the same builder.

faq.q: How should builders plan a play area to protect value?
faq.a: Plan it early in the site layout, choose commercial-grade equipment with durable materials, include proper safety surfacing, place it where it is visible and supervised, and hand it over with a maintenance guide and warranty documents.
